title: Vulnerability scanner activity
description: Web requests carrying the user-agent of a well-known offensive scanner.

title: Web shell command execution
description: Script under a web root invoked with a command parameter - a classic web-shell pattern.

title: Large archive downloaded from web server
description: An archive or database dump larger than 10 MB was served successfully.

title: Sudo to an interactive root shell
description: A user spawned a root shell or changed setuid bits through sudo.

title: Local account created
description: A new local account was created - common attacker backdoor.

title: Crontab modified
description: A crontab was replaced or edited, which can provide scheduled re-entry.

title: Encoded PowerShell command
description: PowerShell launched with a Base64-encoded command, often used to hide payloads.

title: LSASS memory dump (credential theft)
description: A known tool or technique was used to dump LSASS process memory.

title: New service installed
technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
description: A Windows service was installed; review the binary path for legitimacy. Windows' per-user service instances (svchost -k <group>, or <Name>_<hex id> running a System32 binary) and Defender definition-update drivers are excluded - note this also hides a malicious service registered into a svchost group.

title: Account added to privileged group
description: A principal was added to a local or domain admin group.

title: Security event log cleared
technique_name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
description: The Security log was wiped - strong indicator of anti-forensics.

title: Scheduled task created
description: A scheduled task was registered. Built-in \Microsoft\Windows\ tasks registered by the machine account itself are excluded; the same path used by a person is still flagged.

title: LSASS process memory accessed
description: A process opened LSASS with memory-read rights typical of credential dumpers, or through a dump library (Sysmon 10).

title: LSASS dump file written
description: A file named like an LSASS memory dump was created (Sysmon 11).

title: SAM / SECURITY registry hive copied
technique_name: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
description: The SAM or SECURITY hive (or any key under them, e.g. LSA secrets), or the whole SYSTEM hive, was saved or copied - together they yield local password hashes. Exporting ordinary SYSTEM subkeys is not flagged.

title: Active Directory database (NTDS.dit) extracted
description: NTDS.dit was exported or copied - it holds every domain password hash.

title: Registry Run key persistence
technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys
description: A value was set under a Run/RunOnce key so a program starts at logon (Sysmon 13).

title: UAC bypass via shell open-command hijack
technique_name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control
description: A per-user shell\open\command handler used by auto-elevating binaries (fodhelper, eventvwr, sdclt) was hijacked.

title: Windows utility used to download or proxy-execute code
description: A signed Windows binary (bitsadmin, certutil, mshta, regsvr32, rundll32, cmstp) was used to fetch or run script code.

title: Scheduled task created from the command line
description: schtasks.exe /create was run.

title: Windows event logging disabled or tampered
technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable Windows Event Logging
description: The EventLog service was disabled, the MiniNt key that silences logging was created, or logs were cleared/redirected from the command line.

title: Remote thread created in another process
description: A process started a thread inside another process (Sysmon 8), a common code-injection step. Windows' own dwm/csrss/wininit/services threads are excluded.

title: Password brute force
description: Five or more failed logins from one source with no more than 5 minutes between attempts.

title: Brute force followed by successful login
description: A source that just brute-forced credentials logged in successfully within 15 minutes.

title: Password spraying
description: One source failed logins against five or more different accounts in a short burst.

title: AWS console login without MFA
description: A successful AWS Management Console sign-in that did not use multi-factor authentication.

title: AWS root account used
description: The AWS root user should almost never be used; any activity needs an owner and a reason.

title: Cloud audit logging or monitoring disabled
technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs
description: CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, GuardDuty or Security Hub was stopped, deleted or reconfigured.

title: Administrator policy granted to IAM identity
description: An admin-level or wildcard policy was attached to a user, role or group.

title: IAM user or access key created
description: New long-lived AWS credentials were created - a common way to keep access after a password reset.

title: Burst of denied AWS API calls
description: An identity hit five or more access-denied errors in quick succession, typical of probing what stolen credentials can do.

title: S3 Block Public Access removed
description: The guard rail that prevents S3 data from being made public was removed.

title: Cloud storage opened to the public
description: A bucket policy or ACL now grants access to everyone.

title: Mailbox forwarding rule created
description: An inbox rule or mailbox setting forwards or redirects mail - the classic business-email-compromise move.

title: OAuth application granted consent
description: A user consented to a third-party app, which then gets standing access to their data.

title: MFA push bombing
description: Five or more MFA pushes or denials for one user in quick succession.

title: MFA fatigue followed by successful login
description: The user denied several MFA prompts and then a login succeeded - they likely gave in to the flood.

title: Logins from two countries in a short time
description: Successful logins for one account from different countries less than 2 hours apart (impossible travel).
